scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-DHCP01 leasing addresses to a VLAN 80 test client through the core relay and registering the client’s name with both domain controllers.
scene.completeCaption: SBD-DHCP01 leases VLAN 80 addresses through the core’s relay and registers each client’s name with both domain controllers under one dedicated account, with name protection on. Its lease history is kept, course 1.19 backs it up, and course 1.8 takes over its administration.

nodes.name: SBD-DHCP01
nodes.title: SBD-DHCP01 · 10.0.20.10
nodes.description: Built in lesson 2 on VLAN 20 as a member server in the Servers OU, run at its console by SBD Tier 1 Admins. It leases the VLAN 80 pool through the core’s relay (F04), registers client names as svc-dhcp-dns with name protection, and keeps its audit-log copies on its second volume; course 1.19 backs it up.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: A domain controller from course 1.1 and the console for this course’s Tier 0 steps: authorizing SBD-DHCP01 in lesson 2, creating the 10.0.80 reverse zone and the update account in lesson 3, and reading who owns a client’s record.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: The second domain controller and DNS server. The scope hands out both controllers, and the records SBD-DHCP01 registers replicate to both, so either can answer for a VLAN 80 name.

nodes.name: SBD-TEST80
nodes.title: SBD-TEST80 · lease from 10.0.80.100–199
nodes.description: A disposable Windows client VM on VLAN 80, outside the domain. It proves the relay and the options in lesson 2, secure registration in lesson 3, and name protection in lesson 5, then stays for course 1.8’s tier proof.

flows.label: DHCP lease through the core relay (F04)
Secure dynamic DNS update as svc-dhcp-dns (F01)
Zone replication of the client records

chapters.network: Nothing is built yet. SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02 run from course 1.1; SBD-DHCP01 and the VLAN 80 test client exist only in the plan, and the core’s relay is already part of the network.
SBD-DHCP01 on VLAN 20 checks its authorization in the directory and leases an address to the VLAN 80 test client through the core relay (F04). No client name is registered yet.
SBD-DHCP01 now registers the test client’s A, PTR, and DHCID records with the domain controllers as svc-dhcp-dns, and the records replicate between SBD-DC01 and SBD-DC02.
The lease path from lesson 2 stays live while SBD-DHCP01 keeps its audit trail on its second volume. No new network path is added.
The test client renews through the core relay and its records answer from both controllers. The refused takeover shows up in SBD-DHCP01’s logs, not as a new path.
